logic-and-correctness: THEME: logic-and-correctness — wrong values, wrong branches, off-by-one and boundary errors, unhandled cases, missing input validation, incorrect defaults, numeric/edge-case mistakes (empty input, single sample, NaN/inf, duplicate points). For HDBSCAN specifically, scrutinize distance/mutual-reachability computation, minimum-spanning-tree and condensed-tree logic, cluster-label assignment, and outlier/noise (-1) handling.
security-and-boundaries: THEME: security-and-boundaries — authn/authz, injection, secrets/PII exposure, unsafe handling of caller-supplied data, trust of untrusted input, unsafe deserialization, path/array bounds. In a numeric library the realistic surface is unsafe/unchecked buffer indexing in Cython, missing bounds guards, integer overflow in index math, and trusting user-supplied array shapes/dtypes without validation.
concurrency-async-and-error-paths: THEME: concurrency-async-and-error-paths — data races, resource/memory leaks, cancellation, swallowed exceptions, fail-open fallthrough, partial-failure states. Look at joblib/n_jobs parallelism, prange / nogil sections in Cython, memory allocation/free paths, and any except: that hides errors or leaves half-built state.
tests-and-verification: THEME: tests-and-verification — weakened or tautological expectations, tests that assert their own literals/constants, new code paths with no test, stale tests, missing edge-case coverage, tests that never actually exercise the new estimator's contract (fit/predict/labels_, parameter validation, sklearn common estimator checks).
type-and-interface-contracts: THEME: type-and-interface-contracts — casts used where guards are needed, optional/required drift, invalid-state shapes, dtype/shape contract breaks between Python and Cython layers, parameter-constraint declarations that don't match actual validation, return-type inconsistencies, sklearn estimator API contract (get_params/set_params, attributes ending in _).
duplication-and-single-sourcing: THEME: duplication-and-single-sourcing — copied logic, duplicate constants/types, reimplementing an existing sklearn helper instead of importing it, values that must stay in sync but are defined in two places, vendored code that drifts from an upstream single source.
dead-code-and-change-hygiene: THEME: dead-code-and-change-hygiene — unused/superseded/unreachable code, commented-out blocks, debug prints/leftovers, unrelated changes bundled in, files that should not be in this diff, TODO/FIXME left in shipped code.
readability-and-abstraction: THEME: readability-and-abstraction — lying or misleading names, convoluted control flow, speculative/over-engineered abstraction, surprising side effects, functions doing too much, magic numbers without names.
docs-and-comments: THEME: docs-and-comments — stale/wrong docstrings or comments, missing invariant documentation on non-obvious logic, parameter docs that don't match the signature, narration-noise comments, user-facing docs (rst, docstrings, changelog) that misstate behavior or omit the new estimator.
data-access-and-performance: THEME: data-access-and-performance — chatty/sequential access, overfetch, redundant recomputation in hot paths, algorithmic-complexity regressions, unnecessary copies of large arrays, O(n^2) where O(n log n) is available, wasteful allocations inside inner loops of the Cython core.
module-boundaries-and-placement: THEME: module-boundaries-and-placement — logic placed far from its data, wrong-layer placement, dependency direction violations, leaked internals, private helpers exposed in public API, new submodule wiring (imports, __init__, setup/meson) that crosses boundaries incorrectly.
build-config-and-operational-wiring: THEME: build-config-and-operational-wiring — build/CI/config completeness, Cython extension registered in the build (setup.py/meson.build) or not, package data, feature implemented but not exported from the package namespace (or exported but not implemented), changelog/doc wiring, __init__ exports, test collection.
